name: DynamicViT: Efficient Vision Transformers with Dynamic Token Sparsification
problem: Vision transformers compute attention over every patch even though the final prediction depends on only a subset of informative tokens.
mechanism: A lightweight prediction module scores each token's importance from current features and hierarchically prunes low-scoring tokens at several depths. Trained end-to-end via an attention MASKING strategy that blocks a token's interactions, which makes pruning differentiable. Crucially, pruning is UNSTRUCTURED, so the surviving tokens stay contiguous in memory and remain hardware friendly.
speedup_reported: Hierarchically pruning 66% of input tokens reduces FLOPs by 31%-37% and improves throughput by over 40% with an accuracy drop within 0.5% across several vision transformers. This is the rare vision paper with BOTH a FLOP reduction and a measured THROUGHPUT gain - and the accuracy threshold is stated.
notes:
NeurIPS 2021 (arXiv comment; the NeurIPS 2021 proceedings index contains the title). Recorded as the origin of DATA-DEPENDENT token count: cost varies per input rather than per model, which is a scheduling problem for a serving system (batched requests now need padding to the batch's largest surviving token set). Its direct VLM successors - pap records visionzip and sparsevlm - keep the data-dependent idea and move the pruning decision to the vision-LM boundary where it actually saves LM prefill.
